lead: A neighbourhood being renewed, with new public housing and three metro lines.
text: In 1997 a renewal plan was approved because of the poor condition of the neighbourhood, and since 2001 new public housing has been built to rehouse residents of the old blocks affected by aluminosis (a structural decay of concrete). The old blocks are disappearing in phases. By 2017 the redevelopment had delivered 607 rehousing homes, with municipal investment of 50 million euros, and in 2025 the City Council set aside a new plot at Carrer d'Aiguablava, 74-76, for 25 protected homes under a right-of-use scheme.

The metro arrived with line 4 in 1999, line 11 in 2003 and line 3 in 2008, and the neighbourhood has a market, a large park and a day centre for older people. It is sometimes confused with La Trinitat Vella, from which it is separated by Avinguda Meridiana. At 2,505 €/m² and 636 €/month, it is among the most affordable in Barcelona. If you are selling, the average sale price is 15% below the Nou Barris average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 200,000 € on average, and this neighbourhood sits in the middle band of Nou Barris (9th of 13 by price). If you are investing, the average rent is 20% below the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: New public housing, built in phases to rehouse residents of the old blocks.
places: Estació de metro Trinitat Nova (L3, L4 and L11)
